gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Gugi bends its letters like a single piece of wire, with lowercase that climbs almost to the capitals and open-cut endings. Next to it, Noto Sans Wancho feels like thick chalk pressed hard.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection and rounds left unsealed, like a hook that never latches. Noto Sans Yi sits under Gugi, whose heading line holds the steady track of a technical drafting pen.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-squar: Gugi draws its monoline stroke from start to finish, with lowercase that nearly touches the capitals. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square then takes over with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp and a soaring x-height.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-onest: Terminals cut open let the curves of Gugi flow outward. Onest settles in beneath with short ascenders over big bowls and a gentle, uniform line, so paragraphs glide without ink pooling in the turns.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-oxygen: Wire-like and unmodulated, Gugi holds one stroke thickness throughout. Oxygen is the quieter sans, with curves that never close back on themselves and lowercase nearly matching the capitals, so text flows open and easy.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-parkinsans: Distinctive, bold, and cut open: that's Gugi. Gugi grabs attention with lowercase nearly reaching its capitals, while Parkinsans keeps a single stroke thickness and stays crisp when shrunk down.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-pathway-extreme: Gugi makes its r, n and m arches match the stems exactly, giving headings a bold stamp. Pathway Extreme handles the text, with clear openings in rounded letters and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-stack-sans-notch: Loud and open, never curled shut: Grandstander draws plain constant-width lines. Stack Sans Notch backs it with rod-stock strokes of identical thickness, and that shared uniform line is what ties the two.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-prompt: Level, bold lettering with open-cut ends: Gugi keeps a quiet beat with no accents of weight. And Prompt shares that steadiness, its oversized small letters and open apertures making every line easy to take in.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems, spaced wide apart, give Eater its dark, aggressive bite. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong offers the plain sans counterweight, with a high-set x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle.
